patient.name: Funmilayo (Funmi) Adeyemi
patient.complaint: Headaches, burning toes and a brief episode of right hand weakness
background: Raised platelet count noted on a routine blood test last year
Non-smoker; no recent infection or bleeding

diagnosis.exam: Expect 'Which is the most likely diagnosis?' from an FBC pattern: raised Hb means PV, raised platelets ET, and massive splenomegaly with teardrop cells, pancytopenia and a dry tap means primary myelofibrosis. Also 'most likely blood film or marrow finding'.

points: Funmi, 62, sees her GP with **headaches** and lightheadedness.
Last month: 20 minutes of right hand weakness, fully resolved.

steps.title: Full blood count and reactive markers
steps.text: Only the **platelets** are high, and iron and CRP are normal: not a reactive thrombocytosis.

steps.lead: A persistently raised cell line in a well woman suggests a **myeloproliferative neoplasm**: PV, ET or PMF.
Funmi's high count was first found on a routine test, which is typical. Her headaches and toe pain are MPN symptoms.

visual.title: Platelet count
visual.label: Funmi 1020
visual.caption: More than double the upper limit, persistently, with no reactive cause.

steps.lead: Funmi's isolated **platelet** rise points to **ET**. A raised Hb would mean PV; a massive spleen with teardrop cells, PMF.

steps.q: Funmi has had a TIA and nosebleeds. Which MPN causes both clotting and bleeding?
steps.r: **ET**: lots of platelets that work badly, so both thrombosis and bleeding.

steps.lead: Funmi fits **ET** exactly: headache, lightheadedness, **erythromelalgia**, a TIA and nosebleeds from dysfunctional platelets.
Funmi's TIA shows her **arterial** clot risk. In the long term she could progress to myelofibrosis or acute leukaemia.

steps.text: A high platelet count is usually **reactive**: iron deficiency, infection, inflammation, bleeding or splenectomy. Check ferritin and CRP before calling it ET.
Exam rule: **Hb up = PV; platelets up = ET; massive spleen + teardrop cells + dry tap = PMF.**

investigation.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate investigation?': FBC pattern first, then JAK2 mutation testing, with bone marrow biopsy as the diagnostic test for myelofibrosis (the aspirate is a dry tap).

steps.title: Working up a raised count
nodes: FBC: which cell line is high?
JAK2 mutation testing (EPO if Hb high)
Bone marrow biopsy: confirms, and diagnoses PMF

steps.lead: Funmi's FBC shows the platelet line. Next come the **film**, **JAK2**, LDH and urate.

steps.title: Haematology work-up
steps.text: Giant platelets and a **JAK2 V617F** mutation: a clonal cause. LDH and urate rise with high cell turnover.

steps.lead: Funmi's JAK2 is positive and her **marrow** confirms ET. In PMF the biopsy shows **fibrosis** and the aspirate is a dry tap.

visual.title: If this were PMF: what you would feel
visual.caption: Massive hepatosplenomegaly from extramedullary haematopoiesis. Funmi's spleen is not palpable.

steps.q: In primary myelofibrosis the marrow aspirate yields no fluid. Why?
o: Needle placed in the wrong site
steps.r: Collagen **fibrosis** traps the cells: a **dry tap**. A trephine biopsy is needed.

steps.text: **JAK2** does not tell you which MPN it is. The FBC pattern, film and marrow do.

management.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate management?': aspirin first-line in ET, hydroxycarbamide if high risk (older or previous thrombosis), and specialist supportive care (transfusion, targeted therapy, stem cell transplant) in PMF.

visual.title: Age and ET risk
bands: Lower risk if no previous clot
visual.label: Funmi 62
visual.caption: Over 60 and a TIA: Funmi is high risk on two counts.

steps.q: Which drug does every ET patient like Funmi start first?
steps.r: Low-dose **aspirin** is first-line in ET. Venesection is for PV; imatinib is for CML.

steps.lead: Funmi starts low-dose **aspirin**. Over 60 with a TIA makes her high risk, so she also starts **hydroxycarbamide**.

visual.title: Funmi's platelets on hydroxycarbamide
visual.caption: Platelet production is suppressed back into the normal range.

steps.title: ET management
nodes: Assess risk: older age or previous thrombosis
Monitor FBC; control BP, lipids and smoking

steps.title: Treating each MPN
head: MPN
Main treatment
rows: Venesection to haematocrit below 0.45 + aspirin; hydroxycarbamide if high risk
Specialist supportive: transfusion, cytoreduction, targeted therapy, stem cell transplant

steps.lead: If Funmi's disease ever became myelofibrosis, care would be specialist and supportive: **transfusion**, targeted therapy, possibly **stem cell transplant**.
Funmi's aspirin and hydroxycarbamide follow the **British Society for Haematology** guideline on MPNs.

steps.text: Do not give **imatinib** for a JAK2 MPN. Imatinib targets BCR-ABL in CML.

science.exam: Expect applied questions: the JAK2 V617F mechanism, why ET causes both clots and bleeding, and why myelofibrosis causes massive splenomegaly and teardrop cells.

steps.title: From one mutation to three diseases
nodes: Haematopoietic stem cell gains JAK2 V617F
The clone overproduces one or more lines

steps.lead: Funmi's megakaryocyte clone keeps growing because **JAK-STAT** is stuck on: it no longer needs cytokine signals.
Funmi's TIA and nosebleeds share one cause: **many platelets that work badly**.

steps.q: Why does primary myelofibrosis cause massive splenomegaly?
steps.r: The scarred marrow cannot make blood, so the **spleen and liver take over**.

steps.lead: If Funmi's marrow scarred, **PDGF and TGF-beta** would drive the fibrosis and blood production would move to her spleen and liver.

steps.text: Teardrop cells (**dacrocytes**) are red cells squeezed out through a scarred marrow: think PMF.

steps.lead: Funmi's follow-up watches for **transformation**: all three MPNs can progress to myelofibrosis or AML.

mcq.q: Which mutation is classically associated with the myeloproliferative disorders?
Which MPN is suggested by an isolated raised platelet count?
Which red cell abnormality is seen in primary myelofibrosis?

o: Purple finger tips in the cold
mcq.r: **Burning, red hands and feet** from dysfunctional platelets; seen in ET and PV.

mcq.q: Which is the diagnostic test for primary myelofibrosis?
mcq.r: **Bone marrow biopsy** shows fibrosis; the aspirate is a dry tap.

mcq.q: What happens when the marrow is aspirated in primary myelofibrosis?
mcq.r: A **dry tap**: fibrosis means nothing can be aspirated.

mcq.q: Which is first-line therapy in essential thrombocythaemia?
Which drug is used for cytoreduction in high-risk ET?
Which cytokines drive marrow fibrosis in myelofibrosis?
mcq.r: Abnormal clones release **PDGF and TGF-beta**, stimulating fibroblasts.

mcq.q: What does JAK2 V617F do to cell signalling?

points.p: Overproduction of platelets; JAK2 V617F positive
points.why: Giant platelets and clumps on the film.

points.p: Headache, lightheadedness, syncope, atypical chest pain
Venous and arterial thrombosis: DVT, PE, MI, ischaemic stroke

points.p: Bone marrow biopsy: diagnostic for PMF (fibrosis)
points.why: The aspirate is a dry tap.

prompts.tip: Exam thinking: ET = aspirin ± hydroxycarbamide; PMF = supportive and specialist.

points.p: High risk: hydroxycarbamide to suppress platelets

prompts.tip: Exam thinking: switched-on signalling; too many bad platelets.

points.p: Clonal haematopoietic stem cell with JAK2 V617F
ET: excessive but dysfunctional platelets cause thrombosis and bleeding

prompts.tip: Exam thinking: cytokines scar the marrow; the spleen takes over.

glossary.MPN: Myeloproliferative neoplasm: a clonal marrow disorder overproducing one or more blood cell lines.
glossary.myeloproliferative: Describes clonal marrow disorders that overproduce blood cells.
glossary.polycythaemia vera: An MPN with a raised red cell mass, usually JAK2 positive.
glossary.essential thrombocythaemia: An MPN with a persistently raised platelet count causing clots and bleeding.
glossary.primary myelofibrosis: An MPN in which the marrow scars, causing pancytopenia and a massive spleen.
glossary.myelofibrosis: Scarring of the bone marrow by collagen, leading to marrow failure.
glossary.JAK2: A signalling enzyme; the V617F mutation switches it permanently on.
glossary.JAK2 V617F: The point mutation in JAK2 found in most PV and many ET and PMF cases.
glossary.JAK-STAT: A cell signalling pathway that tells marrow cells to grow.
glossary.constitutive: Switched on all the time, without needing a signal.
glossary.clonal: Arising from one abnormal cell that has multiplied.
glossary.haematopoietic stem cell: A marrow cell that gives rise to all the blood cell lines.
glossary.megakaryocyte: The large marrow cell that makes platelets.
glossary.reactive thrombocytosis: A raised platelet count caused by infection, inflammation, bleeding or iron deficiency.
glossary.erythromelalgia: Burning pain and redness of the hands and feet from dysfunctional platelets.
glossary.hepatosplenomegaly: Enlargement of both the liver and spleen.
glossary.extramedullary haematopoiesis: Blood cell production outside the marrow, in the liver and spleen.
glossary.dry tap: A bone marrow aspiration that yields no fluid because the marrow is fibrosed.
glossary.dacrocytes: Teardrop-shaped red cells seen in myelofibrosis.
glossary.teardrop cells: Red cells deformed into a teardrop shape squeezing through a scarred marrow.
glossary.leukoerythroblastic: A blood film with immature white and nucleated red cells, from marrow infiltration or fibrosis.
glossary.pancytopenia: Low red cells, white cells and platelets together.
glossary.blasts: Immature blood cells; many in the blood suggest acute leukaemia.
glossary.bone marrow biopsy: A trephine core of marrow, needed to diagnose myelofibrosis.
glossary.trephine: A core biopsy of bone marrow, used when the aspirate is a dry tap.
glossary.LDH: Lactate dehydrogenase, raised with high cell turnover.
glossary.urate: A breakdown product of DNA; raised with high cell turnover.
glossary.hydroxycarbamide: An oral cytoreductive drug that suppresses blood cell production by inhibiting ribonucleotide reductase.
glossary.cytoreduction: Using drugs to lower blood cell counts.
glossary.aspirin: An antiplatelet drug given first-line in ET to reduce clots.
glossary.stem cell transplant: Replacing the marrow with donor stem cells; the only curative option in PMF.
glossary.PDGF: Platelet-derived growth factor, which stimulates fibroblasts in myelofibrosis.
glossary.TGF-beta: Transforming growth factor beta, a cytokine that drives marrow fibrosis.
glossary.AML: Acute myeloid leukaemia, a possible late transformation of any MPN.
glossary.CML: Chronic myeloid leukaemia: an MPN driven by BCR-ABL, treated with imatinib.
glossary.BCR-ABL: The Philadelphia chromosome fusion gene of CML.
glossary.imatinib: A tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets BCR-ABL in CML.
glossary.TIA: Transient ischaemic attack: brief stroke symptoms that fully resolve.

technique.stem: A 71 year old man has 6 months of fatigue, night sweats and early satiety. He has lost 8 kg. He is pale and his spleen is palpable to the right iliac fossa. A blood film shows teardrop-shaped red cells and nucleated red cells. Bone marrow aspiration yields no material.
technique.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

steps.x: A diagnosis question about a big spleen and low counts.

clues: fatigue, night sweats and early satiety
palpable to the right iliac fossa
steps.x: **Massive splenomegaly**, constitutional symptoms, **dacrocytes**, a leukoerythroblastic film, a **dry tap** and pancytopenia.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Primary myelofibrosis**.

elim: Aplastic anaemia has no splenomegaly and a hypocellular marrow that aspirates.
CML has a very high WCC, not a low one.
ET has a high platelet count.
PV has a high Hb.

steps.x: **E. Primary myelofibrosis.** Rule: massive spleen + teardrop cells + dry tap = PMF.

technique.stem: A 66 year old woman has a platelet count of 910 ×10⁹/L on three blood tests over 6 months. She has no infection, bleeding or inflammatory disease. Her ferritin and CRP are normal. Her pulse rate is 74 bpm and BP 134/82 mmHg.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation to look for a clonal cause?

steps.x: Next test for a persistent thrombocytosis with reactive causes excluded.

clues: no infection, bleeding or inflammatory disease
steps.x: **Persistent**, non-reactive thrombocytosis: suspect **ET**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **JAK2 mutation testing**.

elim: BCR-ABL is for CML; it may be added, but alone it misses JAK2 MPNs.
A clotting screen does not identify an MPN.
CT is not part of the MPN work-up.
Waiting a year leaves her clot risk untreated.

steps.x: **D. JAK2 mutation testing.** Rule: persistent unexplained high count = JAK2.

technique.stem: A 44 year old woman has essential thrombocythaemia confirmed by JAK2 testing and bone marrow biopsy. She has never had a thrombosis or bleed. Her pulse rate is 70 bpm and BP 122/76 mmHg.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate initial management?

steps.x: First-line treatment of ET.

clues: never had a thrombosis or bleed
steps.x: Young, no clots: **low-risk ET**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Low-dose **aspirin**.

elim: Hydroxycarbamide is added for high-risk ET (older or previous thrombosis).
Imatinib is for CML.
Venesection is for PV.
Warfarin is not routine in ET.

steps.x: **A. Aspirin.** Rule: ET = aspirin; add hydroxycarbamide if high risk.

technique.stem: A 58 year old man with essential thrombocythaemia has had a DVT and now has recurrent nosebleeds and easy bruising. His platelet count is 1300 ×10⁹/L. His clotting screen is normal.
technique.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of his combined clotting and bleeding?

steps.x: Mechanism question: why ET causes both clots and bleeds.
Clots and bleeds, a very high count, and normal clotting factors.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Clonal megakaryocytes make **too many platelets that work badly**.

elim: Vitamin K deficiency would prolong the PT.
Red cell hyperviscosity is PV; his problem is platelets.
Immune destruction lowers the platelet count.
Liver failure would derange the clotting screen.

steps.x: **B. Excessive but dysfunctional platelets.** Rule: ET = too many, poorly working platelets = clots and bleeds.

practice.stem: A 60 year old woman has headaches and burning pain in her toes. She had a transient ischaemic attack 2 months ago. Her pulse rate is 78 bpm, BP 136/82 mmHg and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air. Her spleen is not palpable. A JAK2 V617F mutation is detected.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: An isolated, very high platelet count with erythromelalgia, a TIA and a JAK2 mutation is essential thrombocythaemia. A normal ferritin and JAK2 positivity argue against a reactive cause.

steps.x: Diagnosis from an FBC pattern.
Isolated **platelet** rise, erythromelalgia, arterial clot, clonal mutation, normal ferritin.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Essential thrombocythaemia**.

elim: CML raises the white count.
Her Hb and ferritin are normal.
PV raises the Hb; hers is normal.
Reactive causes are not JAK2 positive and need a trigger.

steps.x: **B. Essential thrombocythaemia.** Rule: platelets up + JAK2 = ET.

practice.stem: A 69 year old man has 4 months of tiredness, night sweats and left-sided abdominal fullness. He has massive splenomegaly. His blood film shows teardrop cells and a leukoerythroblastic picture. A bone marrow aspirate is attempted.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on bone marrow aspiration?
practice.e: Primary myelofibrosis replaces the marrow with collagen, so the aspirate is a dry tap and a trephine biopsy is needed. Excess plasma cells mean myeloma.

steps.x: Most likely marrow finding: work out the diagnosis first.
Classic **primary myelofibrosis**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Fibrosed marrow: **dry tap**.

elim: Excess plasma cells mean myeloma.
A fatty hypocellular marrow is aplastic anaemia, with no big spleen.
Over 20% blasts means acute leukaemia.
Ringed sideroblasts mean sideroblastic anaemia or MDS.

steps.x: **A. Dry tap.** Rule: PMF = dry tap; trephine biopsy shows fibrosis.

practice.stem: A 65 year old man has itching after hot baths and a red face. He has never smoked. His pulse rate is 76 bpm, BP 150/92 mmHg and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air. His spleen is palpable. A JAK2 V617F mutation is detected.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: A dominant Hb rise with aquagenic pruritus, plethora, splenomegaly and JAK2 is polycythaemia vera. The platelet rise is modest; ET does not raise the Hb.

steps.x: Which MPN: find the dominant line.
**Hb** is the dominant rise; bath itch, plethora, spleen, no hypoxic cause.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Polycythaemia vera**.

elim: CML gives a very high WCC with a left shift.
ET does not raise the Hb.
PMF causes anaemia.
Secondary polycythaemia is JAK2 negative with a hypoxic cause.

steps.x: **C. Polycythaemia vera.** Rule: Hb up = PV.

practice.stem: A 73 year old woman has 5 months of fatigue and weight loss. She has massive splenomegaly and pancytopenia. A bone marrow aspirate is a dry tap and the trephine biopsy shows extensive fibrosis.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on her blood film?
practice.e: Primary myelofibrosis releases teardrop-shaped poikilocytes (dacrocytes) from the fibrotic marrow, with a leukoerythroblastic picture. Smudge cells mean CLL.

steps.x: Blood film finding: name the condition first.
**Primary myelofibrosis**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Teardrop cells (dacrocytes)**.

elim: Bite cells are G6PD deficiency.
Schistocytes are microangiopathic haemolysis (DIC, TTP, HUS).
Smudge cells are CLL.
Target cells are liver disease, thalassaemia or hyposplenism.

steps.x: **B. Dacrocytes.** Rule: PMF = teardrop cells.

practice.stem: A 57 year old man with essential thrombocythaemia has episodes of burning pain and redness in both feet, worse with warmth and after walking, and eased by cooling his feet. His foot pulses are normal. His pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 130/80 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely cause of his foot symptoms?
practice.e: Burning, red feet worse with heat and relieved by cooling in ET is erythromelalgia from dysfunctional platelets. Raynaud's is triggered by cold.

steps.x: A symptom of an MPN.

clues: burning pain and redness in both feet
steps.x: Heat-triggered **burning red** feet in **ET**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Erythromelalgia**.

elim: Gout is a single hot swollen joint, not both feet episodically.
Neuropathy is constant numbness or tingling, not red flushing.
Raynaud's is triggered by cold, with white then blue fingers.
Venous insufficiency gives swelling and pigmentation, not episodic burning.

steps.x: **A. Erythromelalgia.** Rule: ET + burning red feet = erythromelalgia.

practice.stem: A 70 year old man has had primary myelofibrosis for 6 years. Over 3 weeks he has become increasingly tired with fevers and bruising. His pulse rate is 104 bpm, BP 118/70 mmHg and temperature 38.1°C. His blood film shows numerous myeloblasts.
practice.q: Which is the most likely explanation?
practice.e: A rapid fall in Hb and platelets with a rising WCC and over 20% blasts in a long-standing MPN is transformation to AML. Worsening fibrosis would not produce a third of the cells as blasts.

steps.x: What has happened to a long-standing MPN.
Rapid decline with **blasts above 20%**: falling Hb and platelets, rising WCC.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Transformation to AML**.

elim: CML has a very high WCC with all maturing stages, not 34% blasts after PMF.
Hydroxycarbamide lowers the WCC rather than raising blasts.
Progressive fibrosis is slow and does not produce many blasts.
Splenic infarction causes acute LUQ pain.

steps.x: **E. Transformation to AML.** Rule: MPN + blasts above 20% = AML.

practice.stem: A 68 year old man has fatigue, night sweats and massive splenomegaly. His blood film shows teardrop cells. An attempt at bone marrow aspiration yields no material.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate diagnostic investigation?
o: Bone marrow aspirate at another site
practice.e: Bone marrow trephine biopsy is the diagnostic test for primary myelofibrosis, showing fibrosis in a collagenous matrix. Another aspirate will also be a dry tap.

steps.x: The diagnostic test for suspected PMF.
Suspected **PMF** with a **dry tap**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Bone marrow trephine biopsy**.

elim: Ultrasound measures the spleen but cannot diagnose fibrosis.
A fibrosed marrow will be a dry tap wherever you aspirate.
JAK2 shows a clonal MPN but does not prove fibrosis.
LDH is a non-specific turnover marker.

steps.x: **C. Trephine biopsy.** Rule: PMF is diagnosed on marrow biopsy.

practice.stem: A 64 year old woman with a known JAK2-positive myeloproliferative disorder has become more tired. She is pale with a large spleen. Her pulse rate is 96 bpm and BP 124/76 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate initial investigation?
practice.e: In new pancytopenia with an MPN, a blood film may show blasts or immature cells, suggesting transformation or myelofibrosis (teardrop cells). It is quick and guides the marrow biopsy.

steps.x: First test for new pancytopenia in an MPN.
Known **MPN** with new **pancytopenia**: transformation or fibrosis?

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Blood film**: blasts or teardrop cells.

elim: CT adds nothing to the cause of pancytopenia.
Ferritin looks for iron deficiency, which does not cause pancytopenia.
B12 deficiency is not the leading cause here.
Bence Jones protein is for myeloma.

steps.x: **A. Blood film.** Rule: pancytopenia in MPN = film for blasts or teardrop cells.

practice.stem: A 74 year old man with essential thrombocythaemia had an ischaemic stroke 6 months ago. He takes aspirin 75 mg daily. His pulse rate is 72 bpm and BP 138/80 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate additional treatment?
practice.e: Older age and a previous thrombosis make this high-risk ET, so cytoreduction with hydroxycarbamide is added to aspirin. Venesection is for PV.

steps.x: Add-on treatment in ET.
**High-risk ET**: older, previous thrombosis, already on aspirin.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Hydroxycarbamide**.

elim: A second antiplatelet does not lower the count and adds bleeding risk.
Imatinib is for CML.
Splenectomy raises the platelet count.
Venesection is for PV.

steps.x: **B. Hydroxycarbamide.** Rule: high-risk ET = aspirin + hydroxycarbamide.

practice.stem: A 76 year old woman with primary myelofibrosis has increasing breathlessness on exertion and fatigue. She is not fit for intensive treatment. Her pulse rate is 104 bpm and BP 122/70 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate management of her symptoms?
practice.e: Symptomatic anaemia in PMF is managed with transfusion support as part of specialist supportive care. Venesection would worsen her anaemia.

steps.x: Supportive management in PMF.
**Symptomatic anaemia** (Hb 68) from marrow failure, frail.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Red cell transfusion**.

elim: Allopurinol treats high urate, not anaemia.
Imatinib is for CML.
Splenectomy is high risk and not first-line in a frail patient.
Venesection would worsen the anaemia.

steps.x: **C. Red cell transfusion.** Rule: PMF = supportive care first.

practice.stem: A 49 year old man has high-risk primary myelofibrosis with transfusion-dependent anaemia and massive splenomegaly. He is otherwise fit and well and has a matched sibling. His pulse rate is 88 bpm and BP 126/78 mmHg.
practice.q: Which treatment offers the only chance of cure?
practice.e: Allogeneic stem cell transplant is the only potentially curative treatment for PMF and is considered in fit, younger patients. Transfusion and cytoreduction only control symptoms.

steps.x: Curative treatment for PMF.
Young, fit, high-risk, with a **donor**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Allogeneic stem cell transplant**.

elim: Hydroxycarbamide controls counts; it does not cure.
Transfusion is supportive only.
Splenectomy relieves symptoms, it does not cure.
Irradiation is palliative.

steps.x: **A. Stem cell transplant.** Rule: only curative option in PMF.

practice.stem: A 62 year old woman has essential thrombocythaemia. Testing shows a JAK2 V617F mutation. She asks why her marrow keeps making too many platelets.
practice.q: Which is the most likely mechanism?
practice.e: JAK2 V617F permanently activates JAK-STAT signalling, so the clonal stem cell proliferates without cytokine signals. BCR-ABL is the CML mechanism.

steps.x: Mechanism of a JAK2 MPN.
The mutation is the cause.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Constitutive JAK-STAT activation**: cytokine-independent growth.

elim: BCR-ABL is CML.
The clone does not need extra thrombopoietin.
p53 loss is not the MPN driver.
Reactive thrombocytosis is not clonal and not JAK2 positive.

steps.x: **B. Constitutive JAK-STAT signalling.** Rule: JAK2 V617F = always-on JAK-STAT.
